Take-Two stock has upside as Bank of America sees GTA Online driving long-term growth Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Take-Two Interactive Software Inc (NASDAQ:TTWO) could generate stronger long-term earnings growth than investors expect as monetisation of Grand Theft Auto Online builds, according to Bank of America, which maintained its 'buy' rating ahead of the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.

The bank lowered its price objective to $330 from $368, reflecting a reduction in its forecast earnings per share for the financial year 2028 to $13.03 from $14.13, while maintaining its valuation multiple of 25 times forecast earnings.

BofA argued that concerns about a potential earnings decline in the financial year 2029, when sales of the full GTA 6 game could normalise after launch, overlook the contribution from monetisation of GTA Online, the multiplayer service within the Grand Theft Auto franchise.

The bank expects GTA Online to begin demonstrating stronger monetisation from the first quarter of calendar 2027, potentially prompting investors to raise their long-term earnings growth expectations.

Its forecasts imply long-term earnings-per-share growth of about 15% annually after financial year 2029, supported by increasing spending as players become more engaged with the online game.

In a bull-case scenario, GTA Online could generate about $110 in annual revenue per monthly active user by financial year 2029, still below the roughly $140 industry average for pay-to-progress games cited by NewZoo.

BofA estimates that GTA Online could account for 40% to 60% of Take-Two's earnings by financial year 2029, with incremental operating margins of about 50% helping lift the group's operating margin to roughly 32%, about five percentage points above consensus.

The bank's bull case assumes net revenue of about $4.3 billion for GTA Online in financial year 2029, while its base case assumes $2.6 billion.

Its forecasts do not include potential additional sales from PC and next-generation console versions of GTA 6, leaving further upside if those releases exceed expectations.

Small stock trades aren't always cheap ones. On Oct. 15, state securities regulators announced a $4.4 million settlement involving two Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC) brokerage units and Merrill Lynch, part of Bank of America (NYSE: BAC). The North American Securities Administrators Association (NASAA) said the firms had charged unreasonable commissions on thousands of small-dollar stock trades.

Andrew Angelov / Shutterstock.com
What Regulators Found on 256,000 Small Trades

Massachusetts regulators led a multistate investigation that uncovered unreasonable commissions on more than 256,000 stock trades over five years. The problem was minimum commissions, which can turn even a modest transaction into an expensive one.

The two Wells Fargo units collected nearly $3.9 million in unreasonable commissions across approximately 228,243 trades between Sept. 30, 2020, and Oct. 1, 2025. Merrill Lynch accounted for another $549,000 in excessive charges during the same period.

Affected customers in participating states will receive refunds plus interest, and the firms must certify that they've changed their commission practices. The investigation concerned retail brokerage accounts, not specifically 401(k)s. But workplace retirement investors can face trading commissions through brokerage windows, along with fund expenses and other charges that quietly eat into their savings.

Bank of Hawaii Corporation BOH reinforced its commitment to shareholder returns by expanding its share repurchase authorization by $200 million, bringing the remaining buyback capacity to $268.7 million. Following $20.2 million in repurchases during the third quarter of 2026, management plans another $20 million in buybacks in the fourth quarter. The expanded authorization provides flexibility to accelerate capital distributions, depending on earnings performance and capital requirements.

The decision comes amid improving profitability. Third-quarter net income increased 20.5% year over year to $64.3 million, while earnings per share rose to $1.49 from $1.20. Net interest income increased 14.2% to $156.1 million, supported by a four-basis-point sequential improvement in the net interest margin (NIM) to 2.82%. Notably, margin expansion continued for the tenth consecutive quarter, reflecting higher asset yields and disciplined deposit pricing

BOH's Solid Capital and Liquidity Aid Shareholder Returns

Bank of Hawaii maintains a strong capital position, supporting continued shareholder distributions. Its Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 14.41% at September-end, comfortably above regulatory requirements, while the Tier 1 leverage ratio improved to 8.79% from 8.57% at 2025-end. The company also maintained its quarterly common dividend at 70 cents per share, equivalent to $2.80 annually. It has a dividend yield of 4.3%.

BOH's liquidity position remains resilient. At September-end, the company held $442 million in cash and cash equivalents, and $3.5 billion in available-for-sale securities. These liquidity sources provide financial flexibility to meet funding requirements while supporting capital returns.

Earnings prospects also remain encouraging, with the Zacks Consensus Estimate for BOH's 2026 earnings pointing to 27% year-over-year growth. Expected earnings improvement, coupled with solid capitalization and ample liquidity, could further strengthen the company's capacity to generate shareholder value.

Overall, BOH's expanded share repurchase program underscores management's confidence in the company's financial position and earnings outlook. Strong capital adequacy, resilient liquidity and anticipated earnings growth provide support for continued capital returns. However, maintaining a prudent balance between shareholder distributions, balance-sheet resilience and growth opportunities will remain essential.

title: Accelevation's SkyBridge bookings strengthen Bank of America's bullish outlook

Accelevation's SkyBridge bookings strengthen Bank of America's bullish outlook

Accelevation's SkyBridge bookings strengthen Bank of America's bullish outlook Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America has initiated coverage of Accelevation, a data centre equipment manufacturer, with a 'buy' rating and a $20 price target, citing strong demand for power infrastructure and modular products.

The bank expects adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 56% between 2026 and 2030, driven by rising investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Accelevation generates all its revenue from US data centres, positioning it to benefit from the expansion of facilities required to support increasingly computing-intensive AI applications.

Its 800-plus field service employees, around a quarter of whom are electricians, provide a competitive advantage as the industry faces a shortage of skilled labour.

The company also operates a fully domestic, vertically integrated manufacturing footprint, which Bank of America expects to support shorter delivery times.

Accelevation's expansion into modular equipment offers another growth opportunity, with its SkyBridge platform securing approximately $700 million in bookings in less than nine months after development began.

The bank forecasts the market for modular data centre equipment will expand at a 30% CAGR through 2030.

However, Accelevation faces execution risks as it ramps up production capacity, having completed approximately 1.1 million square feet of a planned 1.4 million-square-foot manufacturing footprint.

The expansion could temporarily weigh on margins, while additional capacity being added by competitors raises the risk that industry supply could eventually exceed demand.

Bank of America forecasts a net debt to EBITDA of 2.7 times at the end of 2026, a higher level than peers, although it expects leverage to decline rapidly.

The $20 price target is based on 10 times the company's forecast 2028 adjusted EBITDA, below the 14 times average multiple for peers using 2027 estimates.

Bank of America forecasts Accelevation's adjusted EBITDA will grow at a 77% CAGR between 2026 and 2028, compared with an estimated 34% average for peers.

Risks include customer concentration, with the company's two largest clients accounting for approximately 61% of 2025 revenue, alongside its limited public-market track record.

Former private equity owner Olympus Partners also retains 83% of Accelevation's voting power, giving it substantial control over corporate decisions.
